content.text: The excerpt condemns capitalism’s poverty, unemployment, exploitative charity, and religious hypocrisy. Owen’s family suffer hunger and illness; after a haemorrhage in the scullery, he contemplates killing himself and his family. Workers endure insecure jobs, dangerous conditions, surveillance, rushed and fraudulent building work, and mutual hostility. Mugsborough’s officials enrich themselves through corrupt contracts while opposing relief. Socialists face violent resistance at meetings near Windley’s Cross Roads. Workers hold a Beano: they travel by brake from Mugsborough to the Queen Elizabeth at Tubberton, eat, drink, sing, and return drunk. Later, in the Imperial Banquet Hall at “The Refuge,” Philpot and Harlow arrange Barrington’s advertised lecture, “The Great Secret, or How to Live Without Work,” amid renewed debate over poverty and political responsibility.
